newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Cocoa seen edging up but resistance looms.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Cocoa seen edging up but resistance looms.

text.p: JULY Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
LIFFE cocoa futures had room to move higher, but analysts warned that tough resistance lingered nearby.

July cocoa was called to open two to three stg higher after closing at its high on Monday when New York's strength spilled over into London trading. New York's July contract reached a high of $1,432 and ended up $17 at $1,430 per tonne. But CSCE July failed to fill gap from $1,432 to $1,441.
July's positive close here, coupled with a triple bottom on daily charts near the April low of 980, was seen as an encouraging sign in the near term.

In addition, "... there's no real reason the rally (in September) couldn't extend to about 1,030," said independent technical analyst Elli Gifford. "But above that, it will run into quite a bit of trouble."
Gifford pegged September support just above 1,000, which she said was crucial because it is a level "on an inclined level of support which is coming in for that potential top to form."
If support held, no top would form and she would expect cocoa to edge up and consolidate.

Gifford said September support just above 1,000 should also hold because it is a level on a long-term trendline extending back to the February lows. She said the trendline has three main points of contact, with the latest made on the June 4 low of 990.
But if support failed, Gifford said September could quickly and easily drop to the February lows around 950.

Some traders expected further pressure to emerge in coming days as speculators liquidated long positions before first notice day in New York on June 17. July's open interest there was still seen high at 17,117 lots on Monday.
